text:
Owen Beck is a fourth-line center getting spot duty in Montreal, and making the most of a small window. The 22-year-old, a 2022 second-round pick, has played seven of the Canadiens' games at about nine minutes a night and has 1 goal and 3 points, one more point than he had in his first 28 NHL games combined.

Seven games is not enough to say much, and the scoring rate (2.87 points per 60) will come down. The encouraging part is the territory: Montreal has 57.9% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on the ice at five on five, about eight points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had his small positive value last season coming on defense, in only 138 minutes.

He was a 51-point OHL center in his last junior season and a top-ten North American skater in Central Scouting's final ranking, which explains why Montreal keeps giving him looks. He hits more than his minutes suggest (15 in seven games). What would change his role is a run of games in a row; so far he's been in and out.
